industry.structure: Travel is sold to end travellers through three routes: suppliers' own sites (brand direct), consumer OTAs (Booking, Expedia, MakeMyTrip) and assisted travel through ~millions of retail travel agents, tour operators and advisors. B2B platforms such as TBO, Hotelbeds (HBX Group), WebBeds (Web Travel Group) and regional aggregators supply agents with inventory, payments and credit. TBO calls itself one of the top 4 B2B travel distribution platforms globally.
industry.hotelsVsAir: Air is commoditised: ~300 airlines carry 80-85% of traffic, 40-50% of bookings flow through GDSs, and B2B take rates are ~1-3%. Hotels are fragmented: of 3-4 mn properties only 2-3% belong to major chains, so aggregation earns 8-10% take rates (Choice, 22-Sep-2026).
industry.demand: Global luxury leisure hospitality spend is forecast to grow from USD 239 bn (2023) to USD 391 bn (2028), HNI segments ~85% of the growth (McKinsey, May-2024, cited in TBO's Jun-2026 deck). India's outbound travel market USD 18.8 bn (FY24), expected ~11% CAGR to ~USD 55 bn by FY34 (Choice).
industry.shock: From Q4FY26 the Middle East conflict disrupted Gulf hub carriers (the East-West corridor), destination choice and sentiment; MEA was ~24% of TBO's FY26 hotel GTV and among its higher-margin markets. MEA GTV was flat in Q1FY27 (+1% in constant currency); India hotel GTV fell 2% as travellers rerouted east to cheaper destinations.
industry.fx: Most international GTV is in USD/EUR/AED; INR depreciation inflated Q1FY27 reported hotel GTV growth by ~11 points (49.8% reported vs 38.9% constant currency) and SG&A growth (12.3% reported vs 4% CC).
industry.globalPeers: Management: scaled B2B peers (Hotelbeds, WebBeds) earn 45-60% EBITDA/GP vs TBO's ~26% (Q1FY27 call).
industry.src: Q1FY27 letter and call; AR FY26; Jun-2026 deck; Choice initiation (22-Sep-2026)

peers.approach: No listed Indian B2B travel distributor. Brokers group TBO with travel platforms (Choice: ixigo, IRCTC, RateGain; Screener: IRCTC, BLS, ixigo, Thomas Cook, Easy Trip) and value it as a growth internet platform on P/E. TBO listed in May-2024, so we use a 12-month window (Oct-2025 to Sep-2026) for its own forward P/E and measure each peer's trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close against its own median over the same window (as HYUNDAI and HDBFS).

excluded.EASEMYTRIP: Travel platform, but loss-making in FY26 and the twelve months to Jun-26 (EPS -0.11 / -0.05); only 26 positive P/E points in the window
excluded.IXIGO: Travel platform, but a Q2FY26 loss (EPS -0.08) pushed its trailing P/E to 254x inside the window (79x at 30-Sep): earnings-distorted, as pharma excludes boom-bust EPS
excluded.ETERNAL: P/E 624-1,759x inside the window: earnings too small to give a meaningful P/E
excluded.PAYTM: Losses for part of the window (35 positive points only)
excluded.POLICYBZR: P/E 72-213x as earnings scale from a low base
excluded.CONCOR, RAILTEL, RITES: Railway-PSU services used for IRCTC; no business link to TBO. Shown as a sensitivity (IRCTC's five-name set) only
excluded.BLS, YATRA, RATEGAIN: Visa services / small OTA / hotel software: different businesses (no screener history fetched)

peers.thin: The natural travel set has only two usable names (IRCTC, Thomas Cook): fewer than three, so per the thin-peer rule we widen to the next group brokers use for TBO, the internet platforms with a usable P/E history (Info Edge, IndiaMART), and use all four names in the base. Travel-only, internet-only, IRCTC's five-name set and a five-name set including ixigo are sensitivity rows.

Bear: reported growth is flattered by acquisitions and the rupee: organic GTV +15% in constant currency in Q1FY27, consolidated +30% CC vs +37% reported
